Task:
Three cache-hygiene changes in the Agent's request building, from the M1/M2 findings.

1. `prompt_cache_key` on OpenAI Responses requests (`ResponsesCodec.cpp`). Set it per chat, from the project id and chat id (find what ids `AgentRequest` or the transcript carries; if the chat id is not available at the codec, say how it got there, keeping the seam small). Without it every JusPrin user hashes to the same cache machines and overflows above roughly 15 requests per minute. The key must be identical for every request of one chat and differ between chats; prove both with a test. Also check whether the JusPrin Cloud gateway forwards unknown Responses fields: if the gateway's source is on this machine (look for an obico server checkout under `/Users/kenneth/Projects`), read the forwarding code and say what happens; otherwise record it as unverified.

On Anthropic the tools come before the messages, so any change to the list voids the whole cache for the chat. Offer `object_import` always, and make a call that has nothing to import fail with the right code from `ToolErrors.hpp` and a message that tells the model what to do (check how the tool is executed and what it does today when there is nothing to import). Test: the tool list is identical across every request of a chat whatever the attachments are, and the no-attachment call fails cleanly.

3. The Anthropic cache breakpoint and skill text. M1 found fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB) sits after the moving `cache_control` breakpoint in `AnthropicCodec.cpp` (lines around 87, 262, 272), so it is billed uncached and only written into the cache one request late. Under the next step of the plan (R2), skills will stay in the record as operator-role in-conversation messages cleared at the next user message, so today's "skills are not replayed" assumption goes away. Analyse where the breakpoints are now and where they should be once skills stay in the record; count, on the 26 scripted bodies in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json`, how many bytes sit after the last breakpoint before and after your proposal. Change the placement only if it is right under both today's behaviour and R2's; otherwise write the recommendation for R2 instead of changing code. # Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (all settled 2026-10-29)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | **decided 2026-10-29** (side session `local_97f342dd`): append-only record of every item ever sent, thinking included, pictures as blob references never inline base64. Visibility is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. See "Roles and lifetimes" below. |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes. Not neutral: the guard test shows that without the note, two consecutive assistant replies merge into one message on Anthropic | **decided 2026-10-29**: notes become operator-role in-conversation messages (Anthropic in-array `role:"system"`, OpenAI `developer`), kept in the record, never cleared; one treatment for project and printer chat. Replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix. |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | **decided 2026-10-29**: visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache. No rolling trim, no silent cut. The compaction is an item in the chat the person can see; the earlier items stay in the record with their lifetime cleared (fits D1), so it lands with R7, not before. |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | **narrowed 2026-10-29**: either deleted (standing prompt already says it) or a turn-scoped operator message like a skill (cleared at the next user message on Anthropic, stays visible on OpenAI). **decided 2026-10-29: delete it.** Keep the injection eval case (live run, batched with the baselines). |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Allowed within one wire format; a cross-format switch (Anthropic ↔ Responses, including JusPrin Cloud aliases served in different formats) starts a new chat or is hidden from the picker for an existing chat | Anthropic docs (preserved-thinking reference, as of 2026-09-03): a model switch never fails a request; blocks the new model cannot read are dropped unbilled, the stored history is never edited; the only cost is one cold cache, same as a thinking-level change. Cross-format is different: OpenAI reasoning items are encrypted and the record is in one provider's shape, so switching would mean re-rendering history, which D1 forbids | **decided 2026-10-29** (Kenneth, forked side session): keep same-format switching, no history edit on switch; R7 adds the cross-format check in `handle_set_chat_model` |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | **approved 2026-10-29** for the phase 2 before/after batches on both providers; the OpenAI "before" run is M4. The prompt-case baseline and the injection eval case are extra batches: ask before running them. |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | **decided 2026-10-29: 5 min for now.** Revisit with phase 2 numbers (how often a chat pauses longer than 5 min). |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | **decided 2026-10-29: add it** (project + chat id); part of R8 |
| D9 | Write cost of a larger chat record | Never measured (searched git, memory, 1,055 Claude and 637 Codex sessions; every timing is for mesh/3MF saves). Closed without measuring: see M5. Constraint carried into D1: pictures stay blob references, never inline base64 in the document | gates nothing now | closed 2026-10-29 |

## Roles and lifetimes in the request (approved 2026-10-29)

Decided by Kenneth in the side session "Chat history cache handoff" (`local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47`), relayed to this doc; his words: "ok. go with your proposal." The provider-doc citations below are that session's, not re-verified here.

**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

**Three roles, assigned by who speaks, never by lifetime:**

| Role | Wire | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| Operator, standing | Anthropic top-level `system`; Responses `instructions` | Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed |
| Operator, in conversation | Anthropic in-array `role:"system"` (Opus 5.5 and 5.x, not Sonnet 5); OpenAI `developer` item | Situational instructions (skills; the file-load reminder if it survives D4) and app observations (notes: slice finished, hand setup change, calibration handover). The doc names "state changes your application observes" as a use case and distinguishes a user message (from the end user) from a system message (from the operator) |
| End user | `user` | The person's words plus what travels with them: workspace block, plate picture, file report. Kept in the record as sent (closes R4) |
| Tool results | `tool_result` / `function_call_output` | Their own channel, never promoted; the doc forbids relaying third-party content through system messages |

**Lifetimes.** Skills and the reminder clear at the next user message on Anthropic (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`, beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`). OpenAI has no clear, so they stay visible and should be kept short. Notes the model replied to stay visible on both providers. Thinking/reasoning is stored per chat and replayed.

**Behaviour changes, so evals are required.** Kenneth confirmed this changes what the model reads. Per his 2026-10-19 rule (last confirmed results are the baseline), every behaviour-changing step runs live prompt evals against a baseline. Baselines needed before any such step: OpenAI journeys (none exist) and the prompt-case set (check the last confirmed model and date). Request-body logging in the harness comes before all of it.

**Risks recorded, not resolved:**

- `clear_at` is a beta feature.
- Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result, so a note landing there needs a placement rule.
- OpenAI accumulates visible skill text (1.3–8.5 KB each); whether that changes answers is an eval question.
- Unverified whether the top-level `system` field and in-array system messages may coexist in one request (the doc implies yes).
- Unverified how the JusPrin Cloud gateway passes in-array system messages through in its Anthropic wire format. Production goes through the gateway, so check before R7.
- Corrections the side session made to its own earlier claims, so the tracker does not carry them: Anthropic does accept system messages inside `messages` on 5.x models; OpenAI's `instructions` parameter inserts a system/developer message rather than sitting above both.

# Provider prompt-caching rules, and where JusPrin's codecs fall short

Working doc, 2026-10-28, for the chat-history cache plan (task M2). Untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.

Both providers cache only an unchanged opening of the request, so an append-only history is necessary on both. It is not enough on either. Anthropic also needs cache markers in the right places, the same thinking and effort settings, and a request within 5 minutes (or 1 hour at extra cost). OpenAI needs requests routed to the same machine, which for the model JusPrin uses means a `prompt_cache_key`; JusPrin sends none. Every rule below was read from the provider's docs on 2026-10-28. "Inference" marks what I concluded rather than read.

Sources:
- [A1] Anthropic prompt caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
- [A2] Anthropic thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking
- [A3] Anthropic preserved thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking
- [O1] OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
- [O2] OpenAI reasoning: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning

## 1. Anthropic (Messages API, `AnthropicCodec.cpp`)

| Topic | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Identical prefix | "Cache hits require 100 percent identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control." | A1 |
| Prefix order | The prefix is `tools`, then `system`, then `messages`, in that order. A change at one level invalidates that level and every later one. | A1 |
| Markers | Caching happens only at `cache_control` breakpoints, or at the automatic one a top-level `cache_control` adds. "Marking a block with `cache_control` writes exactly one cache entry"; no entry is written for any earlier position. At most 4 breakpoints per request, and the automatic one takes one of the 4. | A1 |
| Where markers may go | Tool definitions, `system` blocks, text blocks in user and assistant turns, images and documents in user turns, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Not on thinking blocks, citations or empty text blocks. | A1 |
| Moving a marker | Moving a breakpoint is the documented pattern for a growing chat ("the fourth breakpoint moved to that new final message"). `cache_control` markers sit outside the thinking prefix check: adding, moving or removing them is not an edit. | A1, A3 |
| Lookback | A read looks for an earlier write at the breakpoint, then walks back one block at a time, "at most 20 positions for each breakpoint". A run of consecutive `tool_use` blocks counts as one position, and so does a run of `tool_result` blocks. | A1 |
| Timing | An entry can be read only after the response that wrote it has started. | A1 |
| Minimum length | 512 tokens for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5/5.1. 1,024 tokens for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.x. 2,048 for Opus 4.7. 4,096 for Opus 4.5 and 4.6. A shorter prompt is processed uncached, with no error. | A1 |
| TTL | 5 minutes by default, refreshed free on every read. A 1-hour TTL is available with `"ttl": "1h"`. A longer TTL must come before a shorter one in the request. The lifetime runs from the start of the request. | A1 |
| Price (multiples of the input price) | Writes: 1.25x for 5 minutes, 2x for 1 hour. Reads: 0.1x by default, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. | A1 |
| What else invalidates | Tool definitions invalidate everything. `tool_choice` invalidates messages. Adding or removing an image anywhere invalidates messages. A thinking or `output_config.effort` change always invalidates messages, and on some models tools and system too. Per-message effort (a `role: "system"` message, beta) leaves the prefix intact. | A1, A2 |
| Thinking in history | Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos keep every earlier turn's thinking in context, and the cache stays valid when a new user message is added. Earlier models strip earlier turns' thinking, so messages after it leave the cache. # Provider prompt-caching rules, and where JusPrin's codecs fall short

Working doc, 2026-10-28, for the chat-history cache plan (task M2). Untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.

Both providers cache only an unchanged opening of the request, so an append-only history is necessary on both. It is not enough on either. Anthropic also needs cache markers in the right places, the same thinking and effort settings, and a request within 5 minutes (or 1 hour at extra cost). OpenAI needs requests routed to the same machine, which for the model JusPrin uses means a `prompt_cache_key`; JusPrin sends none. Every rule below was read from the provider's docs on 2026-10-28. "Inference" marks what I concluded rather than read.

Sources:
- [A1] Anthropic prompt caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
- [A2] Anthropic thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking
- [A3] Anthropic preserved thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking
- [O1] OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
- [O2] OpenAI reasoning: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning

## 1. Anthropic (Messages API, `AnthropicCodec.cpp`)

| Topic | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Identical prefix | "Cache hits require 100 percent identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control." | A1 |
| Prefix order | The prefix is `tools`, then `system`, then `messages`, in that order. A change at one level invalidates that level and every later one. | A1 |
| Markers | Caching happens only at `cache_control` breakpoints, or at the automatic one a top-level `cache_control` adds. "Marking a block with `cache_control` writes exactly one cache entry"; no entry is written for any earlier position. At most 4 breakpoints per request, and the automatic one takes one of the 4. | A1 |
| Where markers may go | Tool definitions, `system` blocks, text blocks in user and assistant turns, images and documents in user turns, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Not on thinking blocks, citations or empty text blocks. | A1 |
| Moving a marker | Moving a breakpoint is the documented pattern for a growing chat ("the fourth breakpoint moved to that new final message"). `cache_control` markers sit outside the thinking prefix check: adding, moving or removing them is not an edit. | A1, A3 |
| Lookback | A read looks for an earlier write at the breakpoint, then walks back one block at a time, "at most 20 positions for each breakpoint". A run of consecutive `tool_use` blocks counts as one position, and so does a run of `tool_result` blocks. | A1 |
| Timing | An entry can be read only after the response that wrote it has started. | A1 |
| Minimum length | 512 tokens for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5/5.1. 1,024 tokens for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.x. 2,048 for Opus 4.7. 4,096 for Opus 4.5 and 4.6. A shorter prompt is processed uncached, with no error. | A1 |
| TTL | 5 minutes by default, refreshed free on every read. A 1-hour TTL is available with `"ttl": "1h"`. A longer TTL must come before a shorter one in the request. The lifetime runs from the start of the request. | A1 |
| Price (multiples of the input price) | Writes: 1.25x for 5 minutes, 2x for 1 hour. Reads: 0.1x by default, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. | A1 |
| What else invalidates | Tool definitions invalidate everything. `tool_choice` invalidates messages. Adding or removing an image anywhere invalidates messages. ## 3. What the codecs do today

`AnthropicCodec.cpp` places three breakpoints, all with the default 5-minute TTL:
1. on the last tool (`tools_json`, line 87);
2. on the single `system` block (`build`, line 272);
3. on the last block of the newest `user` message (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

It sends `thinking: adaptive` and `output_config.effort` from the chat's model choice, replays each response's own blocks (thinking included) within a turn, keeps fired skills in place for the rest of the turn, and reads `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.

`ResponsesCodec.cpp` sends `store: false`, `parallel_tool_calls: true`, `instructions`, `tools`, `input`, and `reasoning.effort` when set. It sends no `prompt_cache_key`, no `prompt_cache_retention` and no `include`. It replays each response's own items (reasoning included) within a turn. It sends fired skills only as the last items of the request where they fired, and drops them from the next request. It reads `cached_tokens` only.

        finally:

            response = await client.send(request, stream=True)

            await _send_error(send, GatewayError(504, 'timeout'))

                            'body': gateway_error_event(self.fmt, 'upstream_error', STREAM_ERROR_MESSAGE)})

import os

from typing import Dict, Optional

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured

from .aliases import Alias, Backend
from .errors import GatewayError

# Top-level body fields each endpoint accepts. Anything else is refused rather
# than dropped, so a client bug shows up instead of silently changing a request.
ALLOWED_FIELDS = {
    'anthropic': {'model', 'max_tokens', 'stream', 'system', 'messages', 'tools', 'thinking', 'output_config',
                  'metadata'},
    'responses': {'model', 'store', 'stream', 'parallel_tool_calls', 'instructions', 'tools', 'input', 'reasoning'},
}
# Accepted but never forwarded.
DROPPED_FIELDS = {'anthropic': {'metadata'}, 'responses': set()}
# Where each format carries the system prompt.
SYSTEM_FIELD = {'anthropic': 'system', 'responses': 'instructions'}
# Where each format carries the effort: body[container]['effort'].
EFFORT_CONTAINER = {'anthropic': 'output_config', 'responses': 'reasoning'}
PATH = {'anthropic': '/messages', 'responses': '/responses'}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UpstreamRequest:
    alias: Alias
    backend: Backend
    effort: Optional[str]  # the client's effort id, or None
    url: str
    headers: Dict[str, str]
    body: bytes


def prepare(fmt: str, raw_body: bytes, aliases: Dict[str, Alias]) -> UpstreamRequest:
    try:
        body = json.loads(raw_body)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The request body is not valid JSON.')
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The request body must be a JSON object.')
    unknown = sorted(body.keys() - ALLOWED_FIELDS[fmt])
    if unknown:
        raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', f'Field "{unknown[0]}" is not allowed.')

    alias = aliases.get(body.get('model')) if isinstance(body.get('model'), str) else None
    if alias is None:
        raise GatewayError(400, 'unknown_model')
    backend = alias.backends.get(fmt)
    if backend is None:
        raise GatewayError(400, 'unknown_model', 'This model is not available in this format.')
    if body.get('stream') is not True:
        raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'Only streaming requests are supported.')

    forwarded = {k: v for k, v in body.items() if k not in DROPPED_FIELDS[fmt]}
    forwarded['model'] = backend.model
    effort = _map_effort(fmt, forwarded, alias, backend)
    _prepend_identity(fmt, forwarded, settings.JUSPRIN_V2_IDENTITY.format(label=alias.label))

    return UpstreamRequest(
        alias=alias,
        backend=backend,
        effort=effort,
        url=backend.base_url + PATH[fmt],
        headers=_headers(fmt, backend),
        body=json.dumps(forwarded, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')).encode(),
    )


def _map_effort(fmt, body, alias, backend) -> Optional[str]:
    container_key = EFFORT_CONTAINER[fmt]
    if container_key not in body:
        return None
    container = body[container_key]
    if not isinstance(container, dict):
        raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', f'Field "{container_key}" must be an object.')
    if 'effort' not in container:
        return None
    effort = container['effort']
    if effort not in alias.efforts:
        raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'This effort is not available for this model.')
    body[container_key] = {**container, 'effort': backend.effort_map[effort]}
    return effort


def _prepend_identity(fmt, body, identity):
    """Puts the identity line before the request's own system prompt, or
    makes it the system prompt when the request has none."""
    field = SYSTEM_FIELD[fmt]
    own = body.get(field)
    if fmt == 'anthropic':
        # A string or a list of text blocks. The identity is a block of its
        # own, so a cache_control the client put on its blocks stays where it is.
        if own is None or own == '':
            own = []
        elif isinstance(own, str):
            own = [{'type': 'text', 'text': own}]
        elif not isinstance(own, list):
            raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', f'Field "{field}" must be a string or a list.')
        body[field] = [{'type': 'text', 'text': identity}] + own
    else:
        if own is None or own == '':
            body[field] = identity
        elif isinstance(own, str):
            body[field] = f'{identity}\n\n{own}'
        else:
            raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', f'Field "{field}" must be a string.')


def _headers(fmt, backend) -> Dict[str, str]:
    key = os.environ.get(backend.api_key_env)
    if not key:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(f'{backend.api_key_env}, the key for a JusPrin v2 {fmt} backend, is not set')
    auth = {'x-api-key': key} if fmt == 'anthropic' else {'authorization': f'Bearer {key}'}
    return {
        **backend.headers,
        **auth,
        'content-type': 'application/json',
        'accept': 'text/event-stream',
    }


def error_for_status(status: int) -> GatewayError:
    """The answer for an upstream non-200 status. Upstream 401/403 means the
    gateway's own key failed: a gateway fault (502), never the client's 401."""
    if status == 429:
        return GatewayError(429, 'rate_limited')
    if status in (400, 422):
        return GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The model service did not accept the request.')
    if status == 413:
        return GatewayError(413, 'request_too_large')
    if status >= 500:  # includes Anthropic's 529 overloaded
        return GatewayError(503, 'unavailable')
    return GatewayError(502, 'upstream_error')


def is_gateway_fault(status: int) -> bool:
    """Statuses that mean the gateway's configuration is wrong (bad key, bad
    model id), as opposed to load or a bad client request."""
    return status in (401, 403, 404)
